warnings.headline: A period of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.
warnings.description: Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland, the north of Northern Ireland and northern England on Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas could see gusts of 70 mph or more, but at this time there is some uncertainty in where, and how strong, the peak gusts will be. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.
impacts: There is a chance of longer journey times or cancellations as road, rail, air and ferry services are affected
There is a chance that some roads and bridges could close
There is a small chance that injuries and danger to life could occur from large waves and beach material being thrown onto sea fronts, coastal roads and properties
There is a slight chance of some damage to buildings, such as tiles blown from roofs, as well as damage to trees
There is a slight chance that power cuts may occur, with the potential to affect other services, such as mobile phone coverage
There is a small chance of injuries and danger to life from flying debris

warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Keswick Campsite
warnings.description:
Following heavy rain and strong winds yesterday, river and lake levels remain above flood warning thresholds. Further showers and strong winds will continue throughout today.

Locations most affected will be Keswick Campsite flooding from the lake and the River Greta. 

We continue to closely monitor the situation . 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  

This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Monday 26 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham Marshes to Belton
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham Marshes to Belton
warnings.description:
Higher than normal tides are expected to cause flooding overnight. 

Flooding is expected Flooding is expected from 7:30pm to 10:30pm on Sunday 25th October. 

Locations most affected will be in Belton, Geldeston and Beccles. Roads likely to be affected include Station Road in Geldeston, the A145 and the A146 through Beccles, the A143 at Haddiscoe and St Olaves and the railway line at Haddiscoe. Levels can take several hours to peak. River levels will remain high over the next couple of days. Levels will also be high tomorrow morning, with flooding possible from 6:00am to 9:00am Monday 26th October, due to tomorrow morning's tide. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   

This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Monday 26 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Bosham and West Itchenor
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Bosham and West Itchenor
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding on Monday. 

Flooding is expected for 1 hour either side of Monday morning's tide at 11:00 on 26/10/2026. 

The weather increases tide table values by 0.48 m. Total forecast tide is 5.42 metres Chart Datum (2.68 mAOD) at Chichester Harbour. Strong Southerly Force 6 wind. Flooding will affect Shore Road and a small number of properties in Bosham High Street and Gloucester Terrace. Water will reach the top of slipways in West Itchenor. Monday's evening tide at 23:15 on 26/10/2026 is forecast to be 34 cm lower (2.34 mAOD), with Tuesday's tides lower again, and without flood impacts. Wednesday's midday tide is currently predicted to be 2.4 mAOD, which may cause minor flood impacts to low lying land. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Activate any flood protection products you may have.   

This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Monday 26 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.description:
We do not anticipate the next high tide later this evening, 25 October 2026, to meet the flood warning threshold. However, flooding is still possible from 10:30 PM on 25 October 2026. 

Locations most affected will be Marine Point Leisure and Retail Park. We do not anticipate the next high tide tomorrow afternoon, 26 October 2026 to meet the flood warning threshold. We are expecting higher than normal high tides over the next 2 days, and a result, we may issue further flood alerts and flood warnings.  

We are closely monitoring the situation .  

Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.  

This message will be updated by 10:00 AM on Monday 26 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: North Sea coast at Easington and Kilnsea
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: North Sea coast at Easington and Kilnsea
warnings.description: High tides are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning.  Flooding is expected from 03:45hrs to 07:00hrs on 26/10/2026.  This is due to high tides, strong winds and large waves. Flooding at the coast and overtopping of waves is possible in the coming days due to strong winds and high astronomical tides. Locations affected will be coastal roads, footpaths and foreshore areas.  We are closely monitoring the situation.  Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. Stay away from promenades where wave and spray overtopping is possible.  This message will be updated by 7:00AM on Monday 26 October or as the situation changes.
